Longevity Noodles with Pork and Vegetables

Served at: New Year's Day · Lunar New Year (Chunjie)

Serves 4Prep 25 minCook 20 min

Longevity Noodles, or Changshou Mian, are a staple dish served during New Year's Day and especially Lunar New Year (Chunjie) celebrations. The long strands of noodles symbolize a long life and good fortune, making it customary to eat them without breaking them. This savory, stir-fried dish is a delicious way to usher in a prosperous year.

Ingredients

  • 8 oz (225 g) fresh or dried long egg noodles
  • 8 oz (225 g) pork loin or tenderloin, thinly sliced
  • 1 tablespoon soy sauce, plus more for sauce
  • 1 teaspoon cornstarch
  • 1 tablespoon vegetable oil, plus 1 teaspoon
  • 2 cloves garlic, minced
  • 1 inch (2.5 cm) ginger, grated or minced
  • 4 dried shiitake mushrooms, rehydrated and sliced (stems removed)
  • 1 medium carrot, julienned
  • 4 oz (115 g) baby bok choy, quartered lengthwise
  • 2 scallions, green parts sliced for garnish
  • For the Sauce:
  • 2 tablespoons soy sauce
  • 1 tablespoon oyster sauce (optional)
  • 1 teaspoon sesame oil
  • 1/2 teaspoon sugar
  • 2 tablespoons water or mushroom soaking liquid

Method

  1. In a medium bowl, marinate the thinly sliced pork with 1 tablespoon soy sauce and 1 teaspoon cornstarch. Set aside for at least 15 minutes.
  2. Cook the egg noodles according to package directions until al dente. Drain well, rinse with cold water to prevent sticking, and set aside.
  3. While noodles cook, prepare the sauce by whisking together 2 tablespoons soy sauce, oyster sauce (if using), sesame oil, sugar, and water or mushroom soaking liquid in a small bowl.
  4. Heat 1 tablespoon vegetable oil in a large skillet or wok over medium-high heat. Add the marinated pork and stir-fry until cooked through and lightly browned, about 3-4 minutes. Remove pork from the wok and set aside.
  5. Add the remaining 1 teaspoon vegetable oil to the wok. Add minced garlic and grated ginger, stir-fry for 30 seconds until fragrant.
  6. Add the sliced shiitake mushrooms and julienned carrots to the wok. Stir-fry for 2-3 minutes until carrots begin to soften.
  7. Add the quartered baby bok choy and stir-fry for another 2 minutes until slightly wilted but still crisp.
  8. Return the cooked pork to the wok with the vegetables. Add the cooked and drained noodles.
  9. Pour the prepared sauce over the noodles and vegetables. Toss everything together gently but thoroughly, ensuring the noodles are evenly coated with the sauce. Cook for 1-2 minutes, allowing the sauce to heat through and coat the ingredients.
  10. Serve immediately, garnished with sliced green scallions. Encourage diners to eat the noodles without breaking them for good luck.

Tips

  • For a vegetarian version, omit the pork and oyster sauce, and add extra vegetables like bell peppers or snow peas. Use vegetable broth instead of mushroom soaking liquid if needed.
  • Ensure your noodles are long; some Asian markets sell specific 'longevity noodles' that are extra-long.
  • You can add a touch of chili garlic sauce to the finished dish for a bit of heat, if desired.
